factSheet.title: CNH leadership financial fact sheet
factSheet.intro: Q2 2026 is the latest publicly reported quarter verified on October 10, 2026. The quarter ended June 30; results were published August 3. Keep this sheet open while answering. The personnel-cost row is separately dated FY 2025 and uses IFRS; it is not a Q2 2026 workforce-cost figure. Dollar amounts are USD millions unless marked otherwise. Consolidated results include Financial Services; Industrial Activities excludes Financial Services. Industrial gross margin and adjusted EBIT margin measure different levels of profit. Adjusted profit and Industrial free cash flow are non-GAAP measures; read the company’s reconciliations for their definitions.

stock.note: Fixed closing-price snapshot from Friday, October 9. This is a price per share, not a live quote or a quarterly financial result.

metrics.label: Gross profit
metrics.note: Industrial net sales less cost of goods sold; not consolidated gross profit.

metrics.label: Gross margin
metrics.note: Published rounded Industrial gross margin; distinct from adjusted EBIT margin.

metrics.label: Equipment net sales
metrics.note: Calculated sums: 2026 $1,229m + $468m; 2025 $1,118m + $379m. Includes US, Canada, and Mexico; excludes Financial Services.

metrics.label: Share of Industrial net sales
metrics.note: Rounded shares: $1,697m ÷ $4,143m in 2026; $1,497m ÷ $4,021m in 2025. This is sales contribution, not profit or payroll contribution.

metrics.label: Personnel costs
metrics.note: Annual personnel expense in the consolidated IFRS income statement, note 11. Not a Q2 figure, North America subtotal, or cash-payroll measure.

cashConversion.definition: Cash conversion (%) = Industrial Activities free cash flow ÷ adjusted net income × 100, using the same reporting period.
cashConversion.meaning: It shows how much cash the equipment business generates relative to CNH’s adjusted earnings. Profit and cash can differ because of working-capital movements and investment spending.
cashConversion.example: Teaching example: an 80% ratio means $80 of Industrial free cash flow for every $100 of adjusted net income in the same period. These are illustrative figures, not a reported CNH result.
cashConversion.note: This is CNH’s public 2025 compensation definition, disclosed in the 2026 proxy. Use the company’s stated scopes and adjustments; the example does not represent an official quarterly cash-conversion result.

coverage.title: North America: what the public figures show
coverage.text: North America includes the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Q2 2026 Agriculture net sales of $1,229m plus Construction net sales of $468m total $1,697m, about 41% of Industrial net sales. This equipment-sales scope excludes Financial Services. The public disclosures reviewed do not provide a complete North America gross-profit, gross-margin, total-spending, or labor-cost figure. Sales share does not establish profit or payroll share. Use a North America profit-and-cost report with a consistent period and definition before making those claims; the global FY 2025 personnel-cost figure cannot fill that gap.

questions.prompt: North America equipment sales were $1,697m; worldwide Industrial net sales were $4,143m. What was North America’s approximate Q2 contribution?
options: 35% of Industrial net sales, excluding Financial Services.
30% of Industrial net sales, excluding Financial Services.
41% of Industrial net sales, excluding Financial Services.
41% of consolidated revenue, including Financial Services.
questions.explanation: Add the two regional equipment-sales figures: $1,229m + $468m = $1,697m. Divide by matching worldwide Industrial net sales: $1,697m ÷ $4,143m ≈ 41%. North America covers the US, Canada, and Mexico. This is regional equipment-sales contribution; it excludes Financial Services and does not measure production by North American factories.
questions.discussion: How does a region contributing about 41% of equipment sales shape our business questions without automatically dictating its share of headcount or investment?

questions.prompt: Teaching example: under CNH’s public definition, what does 80% cash conversion mean for the same period?
options: $80 of revenue for every $100 of Industrial free cash flow.
$80 of Industrial free cash flow for every $100 of adjusted net income.
$80 of adjusted net income for every $100 of Industrial free cash flow.
$80 of customer cash collected for every $100 of sales invoiced.
questions.explanation: CNH’s published 2025 compensation definition divides Industrial Activities free cash flow by adjusted net income. In this teaching example, $80 ÷ $100 × 100 = 80%. It relates Industrial cash generation to adjusted earnings, not cash collected as a share of revenue or the cash balance. Both figures must cover the same period. As general cash-flow drivers, inventory growth or slower customer collections can absorb operating cash, while capital expenditure reduces free cash flow. CNH links the measure to working-capital management and informed capital-investment decisions. The example is not a reported CNH result.
questions.discussion: How could inventory, customer-payment timing, or capital investment make cash conversion change even when profit holds steady? Which operational decisions could our team help improve?
questions.basis: CNH public 2025 compensation definition · 2026 proxy, pages 25–26 · 80% is a teaching example

questions.prompt: North America contributed about 41% of Q2 equipment sales. What does that establish about its profit and workforce costs?
options: It establishes a 41% gross-profit share; workforce costs need separate regional figures.
It establishes a 41% workforce-cost share; gross profit needs separate regional figures.
It establishes 41% shares of both gross profit and workforce costs.
Neither share is established; profit and workforce costs need separate regional figures.
questions.explanation: A sales share does not establish a profit or cost share. Product mix, pricing, cost structures, and where work occurs can differ by region. The public figures reviewed do not supply complete North America gross profit, total spending, or labor costs. The personnel figure is also global FY 2025 IFRS expense, while the sales share is Q2 2026 equipment revenue.
questions.discussion: Which North America profit-and-cost report would we request before deciding where to invest, and how would we define labor cost consistently across teams?
questions.basis: Evidence interpretation · public regional sales and global personnel disclosures do not establish a regional profit or cost allocation

questions.prompt: What does CNH’s published $2.827bn personnel-cost figure represent?
options: Global cash payroll paid during FY 2025, measured by the consolidated cash-flow statement.
North America personnel expense for FY 2025, measured under IFRS.
Global consolidated personnel expense for FY 2025, measured under IFRS.
Global consolidated personnel expense for Q2 2026, measured under US GAAP.
questions.explanation: The published amount is $2.827bn of global consolidated IFRS personnel expense for the year ended December 31, 2025. The decline is $102m ÷ $2,929m ≈ 3.5%. It is neither a North America subtotal nor a Q2 2026 measure. An income-statement expense is not itself cash payroll; current regional costs need a separately defined report.
